# CNBC Steve Jobs September 2006

**Source**: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r7wXWDrvj0M

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-26 13:06

---

**[Speaker 1]**: Welcome back. Apple does it again. First came music and TV shows and today the tech giant unveiled its long awaited movie service on iTunes. It allows customers buy movies from the Disney Studios for between $9.99 and $14.99 a piece. Apple also today introduced a new iPod Nano, which is expected to retail for between $149 and $249. Take a look at Apple's stock today. We had a pretty good day for technology, Apple included, up 24 cents, 1/3 of 1%. Over the past year, it is up more than 40%. Take a look at that chart. The products mark Apple's latest salvo in the battle for your living room. See Silicon Valley uh reporter Jim Goldman with more in San Francisco. Jim?

**[Jim Goldman]**: Hey Maria, good evening to you. Yeah, indeed Apple unveils a complete redesign of the iPod and stakes its claim in digital entertainment, a very big deal for the company. In fact, Apple's showing off a new line of colorful Nanos, thinner, more storage and cheaper. The company also showing an almost microscopic new iPod shuffle that'll retail for 79 bucks when it becomes available next month. Apple selling 60 million iPods since 2001, generating $12 billion in revenue so far. And while analysts say sales appear to be slowing, Steve Jobs tells me in an exclusive interview that sales are as robust as ever and he's optimistic.

**[Steve Jobs]**: We're really happy with our iPod sales. I mean, you know, iPod sales are are seasonal. So we're going into the holiday quarter, which is for the last two years uh been our biggest quarter. Uh and um so, you know, we have we have good expectations for how many iPods we're going to sell next quarter, but we're we're in uncharted territory. I mean, we've never sold this many of anything before. And uh and so we're learning as we go, but but so far we're pretty happy.

**[Jim Goldman]**: Well, cue those famous San Francisco sirens as I tell you that Apple also unveiled its long awaited download movie service starting with 75 feature films from Disney and all of its major studios. Downloaded video, a big deal for Apple, 45 million TV show downloads in less than a year, and Apple sees movie downloads as certainly the next big thing. Apple also showing off something called ITV today, a way to wirelessly transmit music, TV shows and again now movies from your PC directly to your television. The $299 box available early next year, what Jobs calls the last major piece of Apple's digital puzzle. Jobs also addressing today the stock options back dating scandal for the first time publicly, forcing Apple to restate its earnings going back to 2001, denying again for the very first time today that the company faces any other investigations other than its own internal probe.

**[Steve Jobs]**: We're mostly focused on on our own house right now. And uh we're not under investigation by the SEC or anyone else. But we did discover uh you know, with all the press around this, we started our own investigation and we did discover some irregularities. And we're, you know, letting that investigation uh have its due due course and and and it will be completed uh in the not terribly distant future. So um, you know, we're not really talking about it until that investigation's done just to give them the the benefit of doing a completely independent investigation.

**[Jim Goldman]**: All of the new products that Apple announced will be available today save for that shuffle, which will be available next month just in time for the all important holiday shopping season. That new wireless television device that really is generating quite a bit of buzz around here should be available sometime during the first quarter of 2007. Maria, back to you.

**[Speaker 1]**: All right, Jim. Thank you.
